definitions.explanation: The tense, threatening atmosphere that someone gives off when ready to attack. Common in fiction and martial arts, and figuratively for a crowd or place charged with hostility.

examples.japanese: {殺気|さっき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じた→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧。

examples.english: There was menace in his eyes.

examples.japanese: ⟦{背後|はいご}→背後：18212_haigo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{殺気|さっき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じて→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧、⟦{思|おも}わ→思う：00492_omou⟧ず⟦{振|ふ}り{返|かえ}った→振り返る：04231_furikaeru⟧。
examples.english: Sensing something menacing behind me, I turned around without thinking.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {殺気|さっき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じる→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧: to sense murderous intent
- {殺気|さっき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{放|はな}つ→放つ：10062_hanatsu⟧: to give off a menacing air
- {殺気立|さっきだ}つ: to become tense and hostile ({殺気立|さっきだ}った⟦{群衆|ぐんしゅう}→群衆：14930_gunshuu⟧, an angry crowd)
- {殺気|さっき}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧みなぎる: to be charged with menace

WATCH OUT:
The homophone さっき means "a little while ago" and is written in kana; {殺気|さっき} is always written in kanji.
